transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Jasper Cole (NorthWind - Head of ML), Rina Matsuo (NorthWind - Platform), Daniel Ortega (NorthWind - Procurement)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, well give folks a minute while they pop in. jasper, rina, daniel — you on my screen right?
[00:20] Jasper: yeah all good, can you hear me? little background noise but fine.
[00:34] Samira: loud and clear. quick agenda: go over renewal numbers, talk APAC uplift and an option for private serving, and then technical checklist - ethan will cover benchmarks. cool?
[00:46] Ethan: yep i'll jump into perf stuff second half, but quick note we brought some new queuing backpressure fixes that help tail latency on small sequence lengths.
[01:10] Rina: good — that's the big one for us, our robotic control is like 32 to 128 tokens, lots of small queries, so p50 is fine but p95/p99 matters more.
[01:28] Jasper: yeah exactly, we care about the tail for closed-loop corrections — a single hiccup means a retry and could cascade.
[01:40] Samira: totally understood. for the renewal we modeled two paths: a 20% capacity uplift on your current dedicated pool vs a full dedicated+private pilot for regulated endpoints. daniel, is procurement looking at a 12 month extension?
[02:05] Daniel: we're targeting 12 months ideally. budget cycle closes end of May, we'd like pricing in a week or so. also need clarification on what 'private' means here — is it VPC-only or on-prem?
[02:24] Samira: good question. private path can be two things: private deployment in your VPC over cloud regions (Redwood Private managed control plane with customer VPC), or an on-prem air-gapped package. both included in the SOW options. big difference is installation & support level.
[02:46] Jasper: for us VPC-managed is preferred to start, on-prem later. latency to apac regions is the other big ask — our factory in Osaka needs good p95.
[03:00] Ethan: we saw about 20–40ms added when routing to eu vs apac depending on region and batch sizes. with APAC regional serving we'd be able to hit p95 targets for the small token workloads, but we need to size GPUs and batching differently for small sequences.
[03:22] Rina: can you size that in the quote? like a separate APAC pool we can spin up for burst?
[03:30] Samira: yes we can include a burstable APAC pool in the quote, with optional reserved baseline. pricing will show reserved vs burst cost.
[03:42] Jasper: also curious about KV cache behavior across regions — if we have requests hitting eu vs apac, will prefix cache warm-up cause extra tail?
[03:56] Ethan: good point. currently the runtime keeps KV cache local to serving nodes; cross-region misses will see cold-kv penalties. we have suggestions: warm-up tooling and pre-cache priming, or sticky routing by customer region. we can include priming scripts in the pilot.
[04:20] Daniel: from procurement side we'll need SOC2 docs, data retention terms, and KMS workflow for encryption at rest. is that standard?
[04:33] Samira: yes we can bundle the SOC2 attestation, and for Private we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and audit logs. i'll attach the security pack.
[04:46] Jasper: any gotchas with SSO/SAML? we want RBAC across teams.
[04:53] Ethan: SSO integrates via SAML, RBAC role mapping available. sometimes team names get munged in auto mapping but we can script it.
[05:10] Samira: ok jumping to benchmarks — ethan?
[05:14] Ethan: sure. goal: run a 48 hour throughput + tail-latency run using NorthWind's prompt set. we'll run hosted variants (eu, apac) and a dedicated instance with continuous batching tuned for short queries. expected outputs: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens. note transcription: sometimes product names get mis-typed, we've got 'RedWood' in some notes but it's 'Redwood'.
[05:44] Jasper: ha yes we've seen that in notes. real question: will your dedicated instance use quantized weights? we need inference costs down.
[05:56] Ethan: we can recommend quantization profiles — int8 or nf4 style — but we must validate quality on your prompt set. the Optimize toolkit will give recommendations; we'll include quality delta estimates.
[06:12] Rina: on the private side, operations: whats the runway to spin up a VPC private control plane?
[06:20] Samira: typically 4–6 weeks if it's cloud-VPC with standard connectivity, longer for on-prem. depends on network approvals and KMS/PKI setup.
[06:32] Daniel: timeline wise procurement wants to sign by end of May. if we do VPC-private pilot we need the SOW in a week.
[06:41] Samira: understood. i'll send an SOW template with three options: reserved uplift, reserved+APAC burst, and reserved+private pilot.
[06:51] Jasper: can we get an estimate for unit economics per 1M tokens for each option? important for our CFO.
[06:58] Samira: yes. we'll send a pricing sheet with per-token estimates and expected monthly minimums.
[07:08] Ethan: for the benchmark plan i'll need sample prompt logs and a small evaluation set (we recommend 500–1000 prompts that hit control loops) to measure regressions.
[07:21] Rina: we can extract that, but may anon the data. also need to confirm data retention — can Redwood purge logs per our retention policy?
[07:29] Samira: yes retention windows configurable, and for Private deployments you control retention. for hosted we can do custom retention windows per agreement.
[07:40] Jasper: question — any known limits on throughput for small token workloads? we often see high QPS with very small payloads.
[07:50] Ethan: continuous batching helps; we can tune Nagle-like timeouts to aggregate. downside is a small added latency. but our routing policies can favor low-latency lanes for control-plane calls. we'll put numbers in the benchmark.
[08:08] Daniel: from a contract point, do you offer termination rights if latency SLAs are missed?
[08:15] Samira: enterprise contracts can include SLA credits and remedy paths. we'll draft standard SLA language; final terms depend on Dedicated vs Private.
[08:26] Jasper: about model variants — sometimes we fallback to smaller models to preserve availability. will that change quality for our control policies?
[08:36] Ethan: fallback model behavior is explicit in the routing policy; we can lock your namespace to specific model families to avoid unwanted fallback. we'll recommend canarying and A/B evaluation during pilot.
[08:52] Rina: networking — do you support VPC peering or Transit Gateway? our infra uses TGW.
[08:59] Samira: yes both, we have diagrams. we'll ask for CIDR ranges and co-lo details.
[09:07] Jasper: i'd like to see previous case studies for robotic control customers — are there any?
[09:14] Samira: we have a short readout (an anonymized case) we can share, i'll include that with the security pack.
[09:22] Ethan: quick tech note — when we run the benchmark, we'll collect traces and token level timing to isolate KV misses vs kernel latency. we'll share the trace outputs and a short postmortem.
[09:36] Daniel: good. procurement also asked about support SLAs — oncall, escalation?
[09:43] Samira: enterprise plans include 24/7 incident support with a named CSM and escalation matrix. private deployments get additional on-site support options.
[09:54] Jasper: ok let's talk numbers briefly — we currently consume about 120M tokens/mo, mostly small tokens. we're projecting 30% growth next year.
[10:07] Samira: ok 120M baseline with a 30% uplift — i'll model a two-tier reserved commitment and add an APAC burst lane. also show what the dedicated+private pilot amortizes to.
[10:19] Rina: any concerns on our side about data residency for APAC? we need logs to remain in-region for regulatory partners in Japan.
[10:28] Samira: we can keep logs and backups region-local for Private/VPC options; for hosted we'll give per-region retention controls.
[10:38] Jasper: one more technical — how do you handle model rollbacks if a new version shows degraded p95?
[10:44] Ethan: we support immediate rollback and traffic split controls. console exposes canary overrides and automatic fallback triggers. we'll show a live demo in the next call if you'd like.
[10:57] Samira: propose next steps: ethan runs benchmark, samira sends SOW + pricing + security pack, rina provides network info and sample prompts. can we tentatively schedule a results review week of 4/28?
[11:12] Daniel: that works for procurement timeline.
[11:18] Jasper: yes week of 4/28 good. also request a short technical deep dive on VPC private control plane integrations — maybe 45 mins.
[11:27] Samira: noted. we'll add that.
[11:31] Rina: quick Q about cost optimization — do you have recommendations beyond quantization?
[11:38] Ethan: yes: batching policies, prefix caching, sticky routing, and request shaping. Optimize will propose config changes and estimated savings.
[11:48] Jasper: last thing, competitor question — we talked to CloudAIx and they suggested edge-device inference to avoid network hops. thoughts?
[11:57] Samira: edge inference is valid but requires ops for model updates; our private on-prem or edge package can support that later, for now VPC private reduces region hops without moving compute to devices.
[12:14] Daniel: ok solid. thanks all.
[12:19] Samira: great thanks everyone we'll follow up with those artifacts. wrap up?
[12:25] Jasper: thanks, bye.
[12:27] Rina: bye.
[12:29] Daniel: bye.

End of transcript.
